candidates.reason: Fast baseline that handles mixed numeric and high‑cardinality categorical features without heavy preprocessing. With only 2.7K rows, a shallow Random Forest trains quickly and gives a performance floor.

Gradient‑boosted trees excel on tabular data with many categorical columns (once encoded) and can capture non‑linear relationships seen in the EDA. Suitable for regression on salary fields and still fast on <3K rows.
LightGBM is optimized for high‑cardinality categorical data and large sparse one‑hot matrices. It often outperforms XGBoost on similar sized tabular problems while staying within the time budget.

notes: SVM (rbf or linear) excluded: would require extensive one‑hot encoding of >30 categorical columns, leading to high dimensional sparse data and slow O(n^2) training.
Neural network excluded: dataset <3K rows, deep models would overfit and add unnecessary complexity.
Logistic regression excluded: target appears to be numeric (salary), making it a regression problem; logistic regression is for classification.

conclusions.recommendation: No model training was part of this run — see cleaning/EDA/visualization results above.
